name: Snorkel Open Benchmarks Grants (benchmark proposal track)
organization: Snorkel AI (with Hugging Face, Prime Intellect, Together AI, Harbor, PyTorch as partners)
description: Rolling grants for open benchmarks, datasets and evaluation artifacts. Expanded to a $30M commitment on 2026-10-07 (from $3M at Feb 2026 launch). Support is mostly in-kind: expert data (clinicians, lawyers, scientists, engineers), research/engineering support, compute credits and hosting via partners. 25+ benchmarks funded (e.g., OSWorld 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0, Agents' Last Exam).
why_fit: Daedalus/Mechanic Composition Worlds (96 fixtures, 1,301 probes) is exactly the kind of diagnostic benchmark the program funds, and its bottleneck (expert-written probes, compute for frontier-model runs) is what Snorkel supplies. The Indic register/'deference floor' work could also be proposed as an open benchmark needing expert linguist labels, which the brief lists as an open item.
eligibility_notes: Program page names independent researchers, domain experts and open-source teams. International/India eligibility not stated; verify.
value_notes: In-kind expert data + compute + engineering; academic attribution kept. No cash amount per grant published.
notes: Highest-leverage new funding channel found. Decision needed first: whether Daedalus becomes an open benchmark (it is currently private, solo manuscript).

name: Snorkel Open Benchmarks Research Fellowship
description: Fellowship where fellows set their own evaluation research question and lead it from design to release with a Snorkel research co-advisor; funded access to experts, compute and engineering; part-time or full-time; fellows keep existing roles/affiliations.
why_fit: Explicitly open to 'independent researchers outside academia'. Part-time format is compatible with finishing the B.Tech (Jun 2027). Evaluation-methodology focus matches Daedalus and the ResonatorLM reproduction audit.
eligibility_notes: Eligible groups listed: faculty, postdocs, PhD students, domain experts entering evaluation, independent researchers. Undergraduates not named; country rules not stated.
value_notes: Compute + expert access + co-advising; compensation terms not shown on landing page.
notes: Application is via a Greenhouse posting linked from the page; posting itself was not read. Treat undergrad eligibility as needs-check.

name: Snorkel 'Red-team your benchmark' service
description: Benchmark builders submit their benchmark to have Snorkel stress-test it for reward hacking, contamination and verifier failures before release.
why_fit: Gives Daedalus an external validity check before the solo manuscript is submitted, a credibility signal that a solo undergrad author otherwise lacks.
eligibility_notes: Builders describe their own benchmark and stage; no other eligibility stated.
value_notes: Free external audit (cost not stated); possible bridge into the grant track.
notes: Page gives no terms on compensation, confidentiality or timelines; ask before sharing private fixtures.

name: Epoch AI - Researcher, Benchmarking Reviews Team
description: Full-time remote role assessing a new AI benchmark at least every two weeks: methodology, what scores imply, task-level inspection, public reports. $100k-$200k (location-adjusted). Applications rolling; 'regardless of background, experience, or credentials'.
why_fit: Near-exact match to demonstrated skills: the ResonatorLM audit (found a sign error), benchmark-validity framing in Daedalus, and the 'deference floor' paper's critique of MT metrics. Strong written analysis is the main stated requirement, not a degree.
location_mode: Fully remote; hires in many countries; prefers US/UK time-zone overlap
eligibility_notes: No degree requirement stated. India not named; ask. Final-year status may matter for start date.
notes: The posting URL resolved on 2026-10-09 but the Lever index listed only 10 roles and did not show this title; it may be closing. Verify before investing in a work sample. Epoch is not in the spreadsheet at all.

name: Epoch AI - Software Engineer, Benchmarking (and open Expression of Interest)
description: Remote role running and maintaining Epoch's benchmarking infrastructure (mainly the Inspect library) and contributing to new benchmarks; Epoch also lists a general remote Expression of Interest across teams.
why_fit: Agent-systems engineering (Maiku 501 tests, ChromeClaw eval harness, ReasonTrace) maps to benchmark-infrastructure work; Inspect familiarity can be shown via an Inspect Evals register entry (see DSC record on Inspect Evals).
eligibility_notes: Same country/time-zone caveats as other Epoch roles.
notes: Salary band from Built In mirror, not Epoch itself.

name: Terminal-Bench (continuous benchmark) task contributions
description: Terminal-Bench is now a continuously updated benchmark (v4.0 leaderboard on Harbor Hub). The README says maintainers are 'actively looking for contributors to add new, challenging tasks'; tasks go through proposal rubric, automated review and maintainer feedback. Earlier guide tied co-authorship eligibility to 6 points (2 points per merged task).
why_fit: Agent-systems and inference engineering (Sefai Rust GGUF CLI, CuteTuner, ChromeClaw) can be turned into hard, verifiable command-line tasks (e.g., quantization correctness, kernel debugging, browser-agent trace analysis). Merged tasks are public, maintainer-reviewed evidence of evaluation craft.
location_mode: Remote (GitHub + Discord; weekly open meeting Thursdays 9am PT)
eligibility_notes: Open to individuals and organizations.
value_notes: Acknowledgment in release; historical co-authorship policy; visibility with Stanford/Laude/Snorkel ecosystem. No pay.
notes: Repo pushed 2026-10-09 (GitHub API). The TB3 call's 'end of May' merge window is past; the continuous-benchmark model supersedes it. Confirm current authorship policy with maintainers.

name: Terminal-Bench-Science task contributions
organization: Harbor framework / Laude Institute / Stanford (contact: Steven Dillmann)
description: Benchmark of 100+ real computational research workflows across natural sciences; contributors propose tasks via form, get domain-expert review, then PR. Target: frontier models solve 10-20% at release. Weekly meeting Mondays 11am PT.
why_fit: Matches the scientific-discovery-benchmark interest and DisCo (Discovery Community) membership; strongest angle is computational-linguistics or ML-systems workflows (e.g., reproducing a metric computation with a known bug, echoing the ResonatorLM sign-error audit).
eligibility_notes: Aimed at practicing scientists; CS/ML workflows count under 'mathematical and computational sciences'.
value_notes: Visibility; API credits for eval runs provided by Laude/2077AI (to the project). Authorship terms not stated.
notes: Roadmap said public release Q3 2026; repo still active (536 open issues/PRs on 2026-10-06). Check whether intake is still open.

name: Prime Intellect Environments Hub bounties (Open Access and Application-Only)
description: Paid bounties for implementing RL environments/evals on the open 'verifiers' spec: Open Access $100-500 for first-time builders; Application-Only roughly $1,000-$5,000+; paid on completion (for benchmark reimplementations, must reproduce known scores). 'Hundreds of thousands of $' committed (Oct 2025).
why_fit: Benchmark reimplementation with score reproduction is the same skill as the ResonatorLM reproduction; eval-harness experience (ChromeClaw, Maiku) transfers directly. Paid, remote, no degree gate.
eligibility_notes: No country restriction stated; payment logistics to India unverified.
notes: Spreadsheet lists Prime Intellect jobs/internship, not the bounty program. Current (Oct 2026) bounty sheet status was not verifiable; repo READMEs no longer mention bounties.

name: tinygrad cash bounties
description: Public bounty sheet (live on 2026-10-09) with $200-$2,000 bounties, e.g., QCOM A630 emulator ($500, no hardware needed), 'buffers and args in any input order' refactor ($300, 'No AI'), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B speed on Strix Halo ($500). Lock a bounty by submitting a good WIP PR. Paid in USDC (or PayPal). The sheet describes bounties as a path to a full-time job.
why_fit: Efficient-inference interest and low-level skills (Sefai Rust GGUF CLI, Superfly token mixer) fit; a merged tinygrad bounty is a hard-to-fake signal for ML-systems roles.
eligibility_notes: Anyone; strict policy: low-quality or AI-generated PRs lead to a GitHub ban without warning.
notes: Many bounties need hardware the person lacks (NVIDIA/AMD GPUs). USDC payment may have Indian tax/FEMA implications; prefer PayPal. High bar and fast competition.

name: Kaggle Community Benchmarks (free model access for custom evaluations)
description: Since 2026-01-14 anyone can build evaluation tasks, group them into benchmarks and run them across a suite of hosted frontier models to produce a public leaderboard; Google lists 'free access to state-of-the-art models' as a benefit; local development via SDK added later; 10,000+ tasks created.
why_fit: Solves the compute constraint (16 GB laptop, free Kaggle GPUs) for running frontier-model evaluations of the Indic register test or a public Daedalus subset, and gives a public leaderboard with Google distribution.
eligibility_notes: Open to Kaggle users.
value_notes: Free frontier-model inference for evaluation; visibility.
notes: Spreadsheet has a generic 'Kaggle Community and Competitions' row (AIO-00176) but not this benchmark-hosting feature. Check model list and quotas before relying on it for the paper's runs.

name: Gemini Academic Program (API credits) via a faculty applicant
description: Gemini API credits and higher rate limits for academic researchers; 'evaluations and benchmarks' is the first listed priority area; reviewed monthly.
why_fit: Undergrads are not listed as eligible, but Prof. Sudip Naskar (faculty, active co-author) can apply for the Indic register/MT evaluation work, where the brief says several runs are still open.
eligibility_notes: Faculty, staff, PhD students at academic institutions in supported countries; India's status is on a separate regions page (not checked).
notes: Route requires the professor to apply; a forum user reported no status visibility after applying.

name: Anthropic External Researcher Access Program (API credits)
description: Free API credits for researchers working on AI safety/alignment topics Anthropic considers high priority; evaluated monthly; credits go to one Console org.
why_fit: Fits only if the work is framed as safety-relevant evaluation, e.g., cross-lingual policy retention of tool-using agents or harness-dependence of capability measurements.
eligibility_notes: Alignment/safety researchers; no degree requirement stated.
value_notes: Historically about $1,000 in credits (FLI, Jul 2025), sometimes more.
notes: Spreadsheet has Claude for Startups and Anthropic Fellows, not this credit program.

name: Cohere Labs Open Science Community
description: Free global research community (4,500+ members, 150 countries) with multilingual and safety subgroups; application open and reviewed weekly; Aya multilingual model work grew out of it.
why_fit: Indic multilingual MT evaluation is a natural contribution to the multilingual subgroup; a low-cost way to find co-authors and reviewers for the register work outside Kolkata.
eligibility_notes: No formal criteria.
notes: Distinct from the Cohere Labs Scholars Program (Aug deadline; 2027 cycle likely ~Aug 2027).

name: Cohere Labs Catalyst Grants (API access)
description: Rolling grants of free Cohere API access for academic partners and public-benefit/open-science projects; focus areas listed as education, healthcare, climate, sustainability.
why_fit: Weak-to-moderate: fits only if the Indic register evaluation is framed around education (e.g., classroom translation), where register/politeness matters.
eligibility_notes: Academic partners and civic/public-impact orgs; probably needs institutional applicant.
notes: Lower priority than Gemini/Kaggle routes.

name: Lambda Research Grant (cloud credits)
description: Rolling grant of up to $5,000 in GPU cloud credits plus mentorship, announced Dec 2024.
why_fit: Would cover GPU work the laptop cannot do (e.g., training Superfly/ButterflyGate mixers, which collapse untrained).
eligibility_notes: Third-party guide says academic affiliation required and a credit card is needed for the cloud account.
notes: 2026 status unverified.

name: Long-Term Future Fund (EA Funds) - individual research/upskilling grants
description: Rolling grants to individuals (including unaffiliated early-career researchers) for AI-safety-relevant research, upskilling stipends and conference funding; decisions typically in 1-3 months.
why_fit: Plausible for evaluation-validity work framed as safety-relevant (harness dependence in capability evals; Daedalus as a world-model failure diagnostic).
eligibility_notes: Individuals anywhere; needs a safety-relevance case.
notes: Details from aggregators; official page not read.

name: Emergent Ventures India
description: Rolling, equity-free grants for India-based talent; 19th India cohort announced 2026-09-19 and included LLM research (e.g., 'research on temporal hallucinations in large language models'), world-model robotics and many students.
why_fit: A Kolkata undergrad with a public ARC-AGI-3 agent, a benchmark and a multilingual MT paper fits the grantee profile; money could fund compute, human labels or travel to present.
eligibility_notes: Apply via EV form and select India under 'My Project Will Affect'.
value_notes: Grant sizes not stated in cohort posts.
notes: Low-cost application with fast decisions historically.

name: Lossfunk Fellowship (6-month paid, Bengaluru)
description: 6-month paid fellowship in Bangalore for early-career, strongly autonomous people to research and explore an ambitious open problem; Lossfunk also runs a 3-6 month funded sabbatical for experienced people.
why_fit: Independent Indian research lab whose themes include 'minds and intelligence' and 'science and discovery'; Daedalus/world-model induction is a self-directed project of the kind the fellowship funds. India-based, so no visa.
eligibility_notes: Typically early-career with some work experience; final-year student timing (post Jun 2027) needs check.
notes: Application link is live on the page but no deadline or cohort dates are stated (form at a binary.so link).

name: Lossfunk Residency (6-week cohort, Bengaluru)
description: 6-week cohort of 10-15 builders/researchers; part-time participation allowed; no equity or fees. Batch 4 projects included neural nets on Atari Breakout, cooperation in LMs, activation steering, agentic forecasting.
why_fit: Past project mix (game-playing agents, LM behavior studies) overlaps with Virgil and Daedalus; part-time option may fit around exams.
eligibility_notes: Builders/creators/founders in AI and science.
value_notes: Peer cohort, demo exposure; no stipend stated.
notes: Next batch dates unknown.

name: Microsoft Research India Research Fellows - 2027 cycle (expected)
description: 1-2 year post-B.Tech research fellowship. 2026 cycle: applications 2026-01-07 to 2026-02-15, interviews Mar-May, start July 2026. Earlier cycles let the CS Head of Department nominate up to 3 final-year students, which gives priority in initial screening.
why_fit: Timing matches graduation (Jun 2027 -> July 2027 start). MSR India runs the multilingual/multicultural evaluation work (Pariksha, Samiksha) closest to the 'deference floor' paper, plus systems groups for inference work.
eligibility_notes: Must have graduated by joining; PhD students ineligible; HIT Kolkata HoD nomination route (if still offered) should be arranged before the deadline.
notes: Deadline is an estimate from the 2026 cycle (2026-02-15), not announced. Nomination details come from the 2024-cycle page; the 2026 page says referrals are not checked, so confirm.

name: Microsoft CoreAI (FoSSE team) Research Fellow, Bengaluru
organization: Microsoft CoreAI - Future of Scalable Software Engineering
description: 1-2 year research fellow role on code migration, code translation and static analysis with AI and formal methods; co-located with MSR India; posted 2026-08-19, applications considered on an ongoing basis.
why_fit: Agent-systems engineering (Maiku, ReasonTrace), Rust (Sefai) and MT-evaluation thinking transfer to evaluating code-translation agents. Ongoing intake allows a start after June 2027 graduation, if the role is still open.
eligibility_notes: Bachelor's or Master's in CS; CV plus at least one letter (letters emailed by referees to the team alias).
notes: Read via job-board mirror of the Microsoft posting. Separate from the MSR India RF program.

name: Google DeepMind India Pre-Doctoral Researcher (2027 start, expected)
description: 24-month pre-doctoral role in Bengaluru with research mentors; requires STEM bachelor's and prior ML research (open source, lab, internship or publication). The 2025-start posting closed 2024-12-18, so a 2027-start posting would likely appear Oct-Dec 2026.
why_fit: GDM India leads Indic-language work (Morni, 125 languages; Project Vaani). The Indic MT evaluation paper plus public repos meet the 'research experience' bar.
eligibility_notes: Indian work authorization; 500-word SOP, transcript, single PDF CV.
notes: No 2027-start posting found as of 2026-10-09; set a watch on Google Careers for 'Pre-Doctoral Researcher, University Graduate, 2027 Start'.

name: Ai2 Predoctoral Young Investigator (PYI)
description: 1-3 year pre-PhD research role, flexible start, no stated deadline; Ai2 provides financial and legal support for visas.
why_fit: Ai2 runs open evaluation tooling (OLMo evals) and scientific-discovery agents (Asta), so both the evaluation and discovery-benchmark interests fit. Visa support makes it feasible from India.
eligibility_notes: Bachelor's/Master's holders planning a PhD within 1-2 years.
notes: Apply via Ai2 open roles; team-specific postings vary.

name: Sarvam AI - Data Scientist, Evaluations (Chanakya)
description: Open role (listed 2026-10-09; first seen 2026-07-28) to anchor the evaluations function for a vertical: build domain-specific eval harnesses for high-stakes use cases rather than run standard benchmarks. Sarvam raised $234M in the first close of a $300M Series B (June 2026) and lists 41 open roles.
why_fit: Directly matches the resume framings in the brief (Sarvam, evaluation/benchmarks) and the Indic MT evaluation paper; harness engineering is shown in ChromeClaw/ReasonTrace.
eligibility_notes: Experience level not checked; final-year timing needs check.
notes: Sarvam does not appear in the spreadsheet at all.

name: Sarvam AI - Performance Engineer (Inference / Kernels), Agent Engineer, ML Researcher (Foundational Models)
description: Other relevant open Sarvam roles on 2026-10-09: Performance Engineer, Inference; Performance Engineer, Kernels; Agent Engineer; ML Researcher, Foundational Models; Product Manager On-Device & Edge AI (signals on-device inference push).
why_fit: Efficient-inference work (Superfly/ButterflyGate, Sefai GGUF CLI) for the performance roles; agent runtime work (Maiku, ChromeClaw, Blindfold) for Agent Engineer.
eligibility_notes: Seniority not checked; some may require experience.
notes: Pick at most one role; the evaluations role is the strongest fit.

name: Ashoka University - Research Assistant positions in program synthesis (ANRF project)
description: Three post-bachelor RA positions (12-36 months) on 'Scalable, Robust, and Trustworthy Program Synthesis' (partial/contradictory specs; SAT/SMT + RL); posted 2026-05-01, 'available immediately'; email CV + one reference.
why_fit: Virgil is a symbolic world-model agent that synthesizes rules from ARC-AGI-3 interactions, which is program synthesis from partial specifications. India-based pre-PhD route.
eligibility_notes: 3-year+ CS undergrad degree, or completing by June 2026; formal methods background valued.
value_notes: RA stipend (not stated); PhD pipeline at Ashoka.
notes: Likely partly filled by now; worth one email asking about 2027 openings.

name: TCG CREST Institute for Advancing Intelligence (Kolkata) - Research/Project Associate positions
description: July 2026 call for Assistant Professors, Research Associates (LLM training/fine-tuning, multimodal LLMs, multi-agent systems, RL) and Project Associates (conversational speech under an IndiaAI Mission/MeitY project).
why_fit: Kolkata-local research employer working on LLMs and multi-agent systems; a way to keep research going locally after graduation, with no relocation.
eligibility_notes: Eligibility, salary and deadline not stated in the circulated post.
notes: Application details are on TCG CREST news pages, which were not read. Status uncertain.

name: EACL 2027 Student Research Workshop (with pre-submission mentorship)
description: SRW for undergraduate to PhD students: pre-submission mentorship draft due 2026-11-06 (feedback by 2026-12-05); direct submission 2026-12-15; ARR commitment listed as Dec 22; notification 2027-01-05; archival or non-archival; registration/travel grants (apply by 2027-01-21). Conference in Athens, 9-14 March 2027.
why_fit: Gives a peer-reviewed home with mentorship for solo work (Daedalus, the ResonatorLM reproduction audit, Virgil), with the first author required to be a student. Non-archival option keeps Daedalus free for a main-venue submission later.
eligibility_notes: First author must be a student (undergrads explicitly eligible).
value_notes: Mentored feedback; poster in main conference session; travel grants limited.
notes: Spreadsheet lists EACL/NAACL/ACL main tracks, not the SRW. Also a possible fallback for the Indic paper via ARR commitment if Kanishk is first author.

name: SemEval-2027 Task 11: VAKRA-Advanced (multi-hop, multi-source tool calling)
organization: SemEval-2027 (organizers incl. Sara Rosenthal, Danish Contractor; IBM email domain)
description: Agent tool-use task on an executable environment of 8,000+ locally hosted APIs in 62 domains; subtasks: API chaining, tool selection from 150+ APIs, multi-hop API reasoning, API + document reasoning. Training data and environment available now; evaluation January 2027; papers February 2027.
why_fit: Agent runtime engineering (Maiku MCP/A2A, ChromeClaw) applies directly; a SemEval system paper is a low-risk ACL Anthology publication.
eligibility_notes: Open; register via Google Form and mailing list.
notes: Deadline is approximate (evaluation runs in January 2027). Needs LLM API budget; check whether open-weight models suffice.

name: SemEval-2027 Task 10: AgentRisk (risk evaluation in multi-turn agent interactions)
description: Task on risk evaluation, identification and policy-guided response in multi-turn agent interactions (listed under 'Agents & AI Tools').
why_fit: Overlaps Blindfold (privacy-preserving browser agent) and agent trace tooling (ReasonTrace).
eligibility_notes: Task website/call not yet found.
notes: No call for participation located; evaluation probably January 2027 like the other tasks.

name: UniAgent 'Agent in the Loop 2027' shared task (INLG 2027)
organization: Univ. Kassel / hessian.AI, Bauhaus-Univ. Weimar, DZHW, TU Berlin
description: Proposed shared task: build agents that summarize all participant approaches in a host shared task and derive structured comparison tables; software submitted on TIRA. Tentative: dataset 2026-10-17; test submissions open 2027-01-11; close 2027-03-17.
why_fit: Agent engineering plus evaluation sensitivity; less central than VAKRA but still useful.
eligibility_notes: Not stated.
notes: Dates tentative until the proposal is accepted.

name: WMT 2027 MT Evaluation shared task - Task 4 challenge sets (expected recurrence)
description: WMT26's unified metrics/QE task included 'Task 4: Challenge sets', where participants build test sets that current metrics handle poorly (breaking -> scoring -> analysis). Challenge sets may target languages beyond the official pairs (none Indic in 2026). 2026 challenge-set deadline was 2026-07-16.
why_fit: The 56,000-translation, 14-language register dataset can be turned into a 'register/honorific preservation' challenge set. That reuses the paper's data, tests COMET/MetricX-style metrics where the paper says they fail, and gets results into WMT findings.
eligibility_notes: Open participation.
value_notes: Inclusion in WMT findings; citations; links with MT-metrics community.
notes: 2027 call not yet out; expect ~spring 2027 with challenge sets due ~July 2027 if the pattern holds.

name: WMT Low-resource Indic Languages Translation task (2027 edition expected)
description: Annual since 2023; 2026 edition focused on North-Eastern languages (Assamese, Mizo, Khasi, Manipuri incl. Bengali script, Nyishi, Bodo, Kokborok), reporting BLEU/chrF++/COMET with no official ranking.
why_fit: Jadavpur's Bengali/Assamese MT history and the person's evaluation framing (metric validity on low-resource languages) suit a system-plus-analysis paper.
eligibility_notes: Open; registration via task site.
notes: Lower priority than the challenge-set route.

name: FIRE 2026 (Forum for Information Retrieval Evaluation) at ISI Kolkata
description: 18th FIRE, 17-20 December 2026 at ISI Kolkata, in person. 16 shared tasks in 2026 (incl. Multilingual Agentic Search, IndicClaimVer, TriMixGen-Indic, VARTA); peer-reviewed track emphasizing early-stage researchers; industry track; PhD clinic in past editions.
why_fit: In Kolkata, so no travel cost. The densest local gathering of Indic NLP/IR evaluation people (ISI, Jadavpur, IITs, industry), useful for meeting potential PIs and FIRE 2027 track co-organizers.
eligibility_notes: Registration terms for students not read.
value_notes: Networking; groundwork for a FIRE 2027 track.
notes: Shared-task run deadlines for 2026 have likely passed; value is attendance and planning for 2027.

name: FIRE 2027 Evaluation & Benchmarking track proposal (organizer role)
description: FIRE solicits shared-task (track) proposals each year, favoring tasks that 'introduce a new paradigm' or 'generate a substantial amount of valuable benchmark data', and especially encouraging South Asian languages.
why_fit: A 'register-aware Indic MT evaluation' track co-organized with Prof. Naskar would reuse the 56k-translation dataset and place the group at the center of the evaluation community.
eligibility_notes: Proposals from organizers (faculty-led typically).
value_notes: Organizer credit; overview paper; dataset citations.
notes: 2027 call dates unknown; 2026 call ran in early 2026.

name: SPAR (Supervised Program for Alignment Research) - Spring 2027
description: Part-time, fully remote 3-month mentored research projects; Spring 2027 applications open 'around December'; open to undergraduates; no country requirement (except US sanctions); unpaid but approved compute/API costs covered. 130+ mentors, 400+ mentees per round.
why_fit: Lets the person work with an established evaluation mentor while finishing the degree; covered API costs address the compute gap.
eligibility_notes: Undergrads eligible; highly competitive.
notes: Spring 2026 applications closed 2026-01-14; expect a similar mid-January 2027 close.

name: AI Safety Camp 12 (virtual, Jan-Apr 2027) - team member applications
description: Virtual 3-month team research program. Published timeline: accepted projects posted Nov 7, team-member applications close Nov 29, teams chosen by Dec 20; projects run Jan 11-Apr 18.
why_fit: Remote, low-cost way to join an evaluation-related project team; no degree gate for team members.
eligibility_notes: Team members open; project leads need prior research experience.
value_notes: No stipend (except a few matched projects).
notes: Upcoming, not yet open: team-member intake opens Nov 7. The page mixes 2026 and 2027 year labels; confirm dates.

name: MATS Summer 2027 cohort
description: In-person mentored AI safety research program; Winter 2027 general application closed 2026-09-06; Winter benefits listed as $19.2k stipend + $24k compute, travel and J-1 visa covered.
why_fit: Funded route to work with evaluation/auditing mentors abroad; the brief's evaluation focus suits empirical streams.
eligibility_notes: Summer 2027 deadline not yet published.
notes: Watch for the Summer 2027 call (historically early in the year).

name: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness - implement and verify tasks
description: Contributing guide asks for new task implementations and especially for checking existing implementations against their original versions; discussion in #lm-thunderdome on the open EleutherAI Discord. EleutherAI also runs SOAR (Summer of Open AI Research), which in 2026 ran July 13-Aug 16 for people with little research experience.
why_fit: Verifying task implementations against originals is the same skill as the ResonatorLM audit; an Indic register task in the harness makes the paper's protocol reusable.
eligibility_notes: Open to anyone.
value_notes: Visibility with eval-tooling maintainers; SOAR 2027 likely mid-2027.
notes: Guide read via a mirror; check the upstream repo before contributing.

name: Inspect Evals Register (UK AISI-founded eval repository, now maintained by Generality Labs)
organization: Generality Labs / UK AI Security Institute / Arcadia Impact / Vector Institute
description: Since 2026-05-08 community evals are listed in a Register (open an issue with arXiv URL + code; a bot validates and opens the PR); direct PRs only from pre-approved contributors. Used by UK AISI, METR, RAND and US CAISI.
why_fit: Registering the Indic register/deference eval (or a Daedalus subset) in the Inspect ecosystem makes it usable by government evaluators and is the toolchain Epoch's benchmarking role uses.
eligibility_notes: Needs an arXiv paper + code.
notes: No paid contributor program found (Manifund funding covered staff).

name: ARC Prize Foundation - open application (no specific posting)
description: Jobs page has only an Open Application ('always looking for exceptional talent'). Secondary reporting says the Foundation was recruiting a Platform Engineer to lead ARC-AGI-4 benchmark work (April 2026). Its 2026-09-03 post says it is 'exploring how to evaluate recursive self-improvement and open-ended innovation' for future benchmarks.
why_fit: Virgil (public ARC-AGI-3 agent) plus Daedalus (world-model failure decomposition) is evidence of relevant benchmark-design thinking; the open questions on harness fairness are evaluation-methodology problems.
eligibility_notes: Open application form.
value_notes: Benchmark-design work at the most visible reasoning benchmark.
notes: Spreadsheet covers ARC Prize 2026 competition tracks (AIO-00049/50/51), not employment/collaboration. ARC-AGI-4 hiring claim is from a secondary site whose certificate had expired (blocked).

name: Unify Continual-ARC benchmark - 'a second seed would be welcome'
description: Continual-ARC (published 2026-09-28) measures whether agent harnesses improve on recurring ARC tasks under a budget. A per-task Python program library beat every harness; ARC-AGI-3 was run once per harness and was 'too noisy to interpret'. Code, run records and paper are pending; the authors say a second seed on any fixed stream 'would be welcome'.
why_fit: Existing verified relationship with founder Daniel Lenton (merged PR). Virgil is a CPU-only program-synthesis agent: a near-zero-cost, non-LLM program-library baseline for the ARC-AGI-3 stream that Unify said was too expensive to run.
eligibility_notes: Relationship-based.
value_notes: Co-authorship or acknowledgment on a Unify paper; a stronger design-partner relationship after the pivot.
notes: See HYP-0001.

name: Basis Research Institute - collaborator invitation (MARA / AutumnBench world-model work)
description: Basis's join page invites organizations/people to work on challenge projects, propose new ones, or join research and open-source development (contact@basis.ai). Its MARA project produced AutumnBench/WorldTest (ICML 2026), a world-model-learning benchmark of 43 grid-world environments where humans beat frontier models. Open roles (Research Scientist, World Models; Program Synthesis) are PhD-level in NYC/Cambridge.
why_fit: Daedalus separates evidence, interface and induction failures in LLM-written world models, which complements AutumnBench's environment-level queries. Virgil is a symbolic world-model agent in the same family as MARA.

name: Signal: ARC-AGI-3 near-saturation and harness dependence (62.7% vs 99.9% for the same model)
description: ARC Prize (2026-09-03) reported GPT-6 Astra at 62.7% (standard harness, ~$26k) vs 99.9% (provider-adapter harness, ~$19k) on ARC-AGI-3 semi-private, and will now report both conditions. A secondary tracker says an open-sourced Kaggle harness reached 55.89% public score by 2026-10-04.
why_fit: This changes Virgil's value. At 2.23% it will not compete on the leaderboard, but a CPU-only, no-LLM agent is a useful fixed reference point for separating harness effects from model capability, which is now the open problem. Daedalus's interface-vs-induction decomposition targets the same confound.
value_notes: Re-targets the ARC work from competing to measurement methodology.
notes: Observation (A); implication for Virgil is inference. Spreadsheet's ARC Prize 2026 rows should be re-scored in light of this.

name: Signal: crowding in executable world-model agents for ARC-AGI-3
description: Two 2026 papers (arXiv 2605.05138, 2607.15439) build coding agents that maintain executable Python world models for ARC-AGI-3. The follow-up reports a fixed-interface verification variant that fully solves all public games (~99% RHAE) with a newer model, and itself flags fixed interfaces/templates as a confound and held-out performance as untested.
why_fit: Overlaps directly with Daedalus ('LLM-written world models', interface vs induction failures). Risk: being scooped. Opportunity: Daedalus offers the controlled decomposition these papers say they lack.
value_notes: Shapes Daedalus framing and related-work positioning before submission.
notes: Code at GitHub astroseger/arc-3-agents-baseline1 (per paper).
